newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RAVANELLI SCORES FOUR AS MIDDLESBROUGH PROSPER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAVANELLI SCORES FOUR AS MIDDLESBROUGH PROSPER.

text.p: Fabrizio Ravanelli added to his growing English reputation by scoring four times as Middlesbrough thrashed Hereford 7-0 in a League Cup second round, first leg tie on Wednesday.
The Italian striker took his goal tally for the season to 10 as his multi-national team ran riot, Brazilian pair Emerson and Branco also finding the opposition net.
Several premier league sides had much tougher evenings, with Leeds, Everton and Sheffield Wednesday all facing awkward away second leg games if they want to progress.

George Graham's frustrating start as Leeds manager continued when third division Darlington held his side to a 2-2 draw, Everton had to come from behind to secure a 1-1 draw with York and Wednesday were forced to settle for the same scoreline against Oxford.
West Ham were also held to a 1-1 draw at Barnet, a goal from Tony Cottee 12 minutes from the end saving their blushes, and Coventry left it even later against Midlands neighbours Birmingham.
Only two minutes remained when Liam Daish equalised for Coventry to salvage the night's fourth 1-1 draw.

Ruud Gullit's Chelsea side looked set for an awkward time when they went behind at Blackpool to Northern Ireland international James Quinn, but ultimately scored a comfortable win with goals from Jody Morris, Dan Petrescu, Mark Hughes and John Spencer.
